stem:
The diagram shows a polygon drawn on a $1\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ grid. Aditya wants its area in square centimetres.

Which claim correctly tells how to find the area?

options.text: Divide the polygon into triangles, find the area of each triangle, and add those areas.
Report the word polygon as the area of the shape on the grid.
Dividing into triangles is what creates the polygon on the grid.
The area equals $1$ because the grid is labelled $1\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Any polygon’s area is the sum of the areas of triangles that fill it. Naming polygon, reversing divide-and-create, or grabbing the printed 1 cm² all miss that hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote the source grid quadrilateral as a pentagon on a 1 cm² grid matching the stem.
